title: Start with a question, then SELECT
summary: An example note on choosing columns and naming a result clearly.

content.text: Example lesson: a query is a precise request for a table of results. SELECT chooses the columns; FROM names the table. The table below is a hypothetical teaching example, not personal or project data.
Name the question before writing the query. Here, the question is: which country is associated with each customer? Avoid SELECT * when you only need a few columns.
Try it: write a query that selects product_id and unit_price from a hypothetical products table. No database runs on this page.
